config.notes: Only address.country changed from the previous proposal, per reviewer feedback. Country pipeline: trim -> collapse_whitespace -> shape gate (letters, space, apostrophe, hyphen, full stop only) -> upper -> map_enum with passthrough for other genuine country names. 'Australia'/'AUSTRALIA'/'Australia.'/'AU'/'AUS' -> 'AU'; 'Singapore' stays 'SINGAPORE'; values containing digits (e.g. 'WA 6105') fail the shape gate and emit nothing for that row. Everything else is unchanged: entity.status is NOT mapped (no per-row status column; asserting 'active' would be guesswork), entity_type not mapped (Incorporated/Ltd/Trust are name text, not a structured type), no per-row observation date so observed_at falls back to resource last-modified, address is a business/contact address. Known source defects carried over unchanged: ABN blank in ~0.6% of rows (record_id is content_hash for that reason) and one 6-digit Postcode that fails validation by design.

fields.reason: Column is the ACNC registered legal name; all held-out values (including 'The Trustee for the Scott Martyn Foundation', 'UCA - Mt Dromedary Parish', 'Project 166 Trust') read as registered legal names, and trading names are kept in a separate column/path.

Correctly sourced from the 'other names' column, distinct from legal name; held-out values ('Walker Close Community Centre', "Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.") are plausible trading/display names and nulls are suppressed.

All 11 held-out ABNs are 11 digits and emitted unchanged; the abn transform is claimed to checksum-validate. Note the record grain is not ABN-unique, so this is an attribute not an identity key — consistent with the stated rationale.

Source values mix bare domains ('www.marradhali.com.au') and full URLs ('https://empowersportsfound.wixsite.com/mysite'), and observations are emitted verbatim. The website transform evidently does not normalise to a scheme-prefixed URL, so the canonical field type is not applied uniformly; downstream equality/dedup on website will be inconsistent.

DD/MM/YYYY parsing is correct for this source: '03/12/2012' -> 2012-12-03 and '11/10/2023' -> 2023-10-11 match ACNC register semantics (many entities registered at the 3 Dec 2012 ACNC start), so no month/day swap.

Concatenating street lines is fine, but Address_Type is uniformly 'Business' and some values are PO boxes / venue names ('Community Centre', 'Egan Park'), i.e. a postal-or-contact address, not premises. It is mapped straight into the generic address.full without any qualifier, and the rationale's claim that this is 'business/contact address' is not visible in the canonical output — risk of postal-vs-premises confusion.

Direct suburb/town field; held-out values pass through with whitespace collapse. Case is preserved ('sunbury', 'DONNYBROOK', 'Goowa'), which is acceptable for a raw string field though not normalised.
Held-out 'SA ' (trailing space) normalises to SA and 'NSW'/'VIC'/'WA'/'QLD' map correctly; enum values come from an explicit column rather than being guessed.
4-digit AU postcodes preserved; state/postcode pairs are consistent in all held-out rows.

Row 2 has Country='Austria' on an otherwise entirely Australian record (VIC, 3025, Operating_Countries=AUS) and it is emitted as the country 'AUSTRIA'. Whether or not that is a source typo, the mapping passes through arbitrary country strings, so address.country no longer reliably means 'the entity's address country' in the AU-centric dataset; at minimum non-AU values should be flagged/quarantined rather than emitted as confidence-equal. The shape-gating fix also silently nulls state+postcode typos without surfacing them.

missed.reason: ISO3 list of countries of operation (mostly 'AUS') — a defensible cross-check/fallback for address.country when Country is blank or implausible (e.g. the 'Austria' row), rather than being left entirely unmapped.
Not a true match, but it is an entity-classification attribute with no home; call this out explicitly as a gap in the ontology rather than dismissing it.

Correctly not used for registration date, but note that rows where Registration_Date is missing could otherwise be mistakenly back-filled from this column; it should be flagged as a near-miss for lineage.

A single constant 'Business' is used to justify treating address.full as a business/postal address; even though it has no enum target, it is the evidence needed to disambiguate postal vs premises and deserves an explicit 'qualifier' note rather than being listed as irrelevant.

critic.summary: Core identity fields are sound: legal_name vs trading_name are correctly separated, ABN shape/validation passes on all held-out rows, and date_registered uses the correct DD/MM/YYYY interpretation with no day/month swap. The main substantive problem is address.country: it emits 'AUSTRIA' for a fully Australian record and generally passes through arbitrary strings, so the field no longer reliably means the entity's address country; the shape-gating also drops malformed values silently. Secondary issues: address.full is a postal/contact-style address (PO boxes, venue names, Address_Type='Business') mapped into the generic address field without any qualifier, and Charity_Website values are not normalised so website is inconsistently typed. Locality/state/postcode are clean. Operating_Countries is an obvious candidate to support or sanity-check address.country and should not be entirely unmapped.

config.grain_rationale: One row per ACNC-registered charity; the record describes the registered legal entity plus the single contact address it lodged with the ACNC. ABN is not guaranteed unique (duplicates/blanks occur), so record identity is content-derived.

record_id.rationale: ABN is blank in ~0.6% of rows and repeats for some entities, so it is not a reliable unique key; hash the full record content instead.

fields.rationale: Column explicitly named Charity_Legal_Name on the ACNC register = registered legal name.
Other names the charity is known by (trading/display names), explicitly separate from the legal name column.
ABN column; 100% checksum-valid in discovery, 1173/1173 held-out values passed.

Charity_Website mixes bare domains, http(s) URLs and free text. Fix for hold-out WEBSITE_INVALID: extract the FIRST URL/domain token, then hard-validate that the token as a whole is a URL/domain, so multi-URL prose blobs drop instead of erroring.
ACNC registration date; DD/MM/YYYY confirmed by the 03/12/2012 ACNC-commencement spike. Does not fall back to Date_Organisation_Established.

Address lines combined into ONE contact address. Address_Type is uniformly 'Business' and values include PO boxes ('Po Box 576'), venue names ('Egan Park', 'Community Centre') and locality-only entries, so this is a postal/contact address, not confirmed premises. Confidence lowered to 0.55 because postal-vs-premises is unresolvable from this source; structured locality/state/postcode are mapped separately from their own columns.
Town/city (suburb) field; case preserved as sourced.
Australian state abbreviations; trimmed first so held-out 'SA ' normalises; unknown maps to OTHER.
4-digit AU postcodes. Hold-out rejects were a 5-digit '80571' and a town name 'Cloverdale'; a strict 4-digit token extraction now drops those rows rather than erroring.

Critic fix: address.country emits ONLY 'AU'. The register is Australian (ACNC) and its non-AU Country values are demonstrably source errors (hold-out row 2: Country='Austria' on a VIC/3025/AUS record). A row-level 'when' gate restricts emission to recognised Australian spellings, so 'Austria', 'Singapore' and 'WA 6105' are left unmapped for that row instead of being emitted as a country or raising ENUM_UNMAPPED.

config.notes: Hold-out fixes: (1) entity.website — the invalid value was a prose blob containing two URLs and a parenthesised domain; now the first URL/domain token is extracted and hard-validated, so blobs drop instead of erroring (no error observed on discovery). (2) address.postcode — hold-out rejects were '80571' (5 digits) and 'Cloverdale' (a town); a strict 4-digit token extraction now leaves those rows unmapped rather than erroring. (3) address.country — formerly passthrough, which emitted 'AUSTRIA' for a record whose State/Postcode/Operating_Countries are all Australian; now gated by a row-level 'when' on recognised Australian spellings and emitted only as 'AU', so non-AU values (source typos) are left unmapped for that row. Judgement calls I did NOT change: Operating_Countries stays unmapped (it is countries of operation, not address country — using it as an address fallback would be a category error and would re-inject foreign values now that the field is AU-only); Charity_Size stays unmapped as a stated ontology gap (no valid target; entity.industry_code would be wrong); Date_Organisation_Established flagged as a lineage near-miss so nobody back-fills date_registered from it; Address_Type documented as the postal-vs-premises qualifier explaining address.full's lowered confidence (0.55). entity.status not mapped: no per-row status column. entity_type not mapped: suffixes in the name are text, not a structured type field. No per-row observation date; fallback to resource last-modified.

fields.reason: Source column is explicitly the ACNC registered charity legal name; values are legal-entity names (including 'The Trustee for the Scott Martyn Foundation', 'Walker Close & Brooklyn Hall Association Incorporated'), not trading/display names. Whitespace collapse on 'UCA -  Mt Dromedary Parish' is cosmetic only.

Held-out rows emit 'Walker Close Community Centre' and "Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc." — both are genuine alternate/display names distinct from the legal name column, and rows with null emit nothing. No sign of contact-person names or licence numbers leaking in.
All 12 held-out values are 11 digits and emitted verbatim matched to the source; the stated checksum step is appropriate for ABN and the mapping does not conflate ABN with ACN or other identifiers.

Bare domains ('www.marradhali.com.au', 'www.holytrinitybalaclavaandelwood.com.au'), paths ('https://empowersportsfound.wixsite.com/mysite'), and trailing-slash URLs all preserved correctly; null sources emit nothing rather than an empty value. Extraction of the single domain token is consistent with the target meaning.

DD/MM/YYYY confirmed by multiple rows: 11/10/2023→2023-10-11, 21/06/2024→2024-06-21, 13/11/2016→2016-11-13, 03/12/2012→2012-12-03. No month/day transposition (no value has both components ≤12 with an implausible flip), and Date_Organisation_Established is correctly not used as fallback (e.g. row 2: 13/11/2006 vs Registration 03/12/2012).

Values are assembled sensibly and match the source, but this is a postal/contact address: Address_Type is a constant 'Business', and held-out examples include venue names with no street number ('Egan Park', 'Community Centre'). Nothing in the observation signals postal-vs-premises, so downstream cannot distinguish it from premises. Also '5 Thomas Terrace, Gawler, SA , 5118' carries the untrimmed source 'SA ' (double space before comma) because State is concatenated before the trim applies — an output-quality defect, not just a qualifier gap.
Directly maps the suburb/town field; case preserved as sourced ('sunbury', 'DONNYBROOK', 'Goowa') which is faithful, and 'Goowa' is a source misspelling of Goolwa, not a mapping error.
Abbreviations map cleanly to the enum; the 'SA ' (trailing space) held-out value normalises to SA as claimed, confirming the trim-before-state step works. No enum guesses observed.
All held-out values are 4-digit AU postcodes emitted verbatim; strict 4-digit token extraction is right for dropping 5-digit foreign-looking values rather than coercing them.

Emitting only 'AU' is defensible for an ACNC register, and suppressing 'Austria' on a VIC/3025 row is a reasonable data-quality call. But the record for Walker Close (Country='Austria') simply drops address.country with no flag, so a possibly genuine foreign contact address becomes indistinguishable from a normal domestic row—the default-DAU plus gate silently hides the conflict instead of qualifying it. Held-out rows confirm AU for 'australia'/'Australia', which is fine.

missed.reason: Not a separate ontology field, but it is the only evidence qualifier for the address block; leaving it entirely unmapped (only mentioned in rationale) is why address.full cannot be interpreted as premises vs postal. At minimum it should be recorded as a qualifier/provenance note on address.full.
Correctly refused as a category error — flagging only to confirm it should NOT be mapped there; it is a genuine ontology gap, not a missed mapping. (Listed for completeness, no action.)

Correctly rejected as a fallback (operation footprint ≠ address), but note the asymmetric handling: foreign operation-country codes are dropped silently, the same silent-drop pattern that hides the 'Austria' row. Keep unmapped; the issue is the lack of a conflict flag, not the mapping.

critic.summary: Core identity and date/address field mappings are sound: legal_name comes from the explicitly-named legal-name column with trading names kept separate, ABN is length/checksum-checked and not confused with ACN, DD/MM/YYYY parsing is verified against several rows with no day/month transposition, and website/postcode/state normalisation all behave on rare held-out values. Two doubts: address.full is a contact address including venue names and PO-box-style entries with no premises qualifier, and it leaks an untrimmed 'SA ' into the concatenation ('Gawler, SA , 5118'); and address.country's AU-only gate silently swallows the one contradictory 'Austria' row instead of flagging it. The unmapped list is mostly legitimate (purpose/beneficiary flags, state operation flags, Charity_Size as an ontology gap), and the deliberate non-use of Date_Organisation_Established as a registration-date fallback is correct.

human_feedback: address.country still leaks bad values: 'Australia.' (trailing full stop) is emitted as 'AUSTRALIA.' instead of 'AU', and a source error ('WA 6105', a state+postcode typed into Country) is passed through as a country. Normalise punctuation before the lookup and only pass through values that look like country names (letters and spaces); leave anything else unmapped for that row. Change nothing else.
